title: Proverbs Chapter 25 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Proverbs chapter 25 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Proverbs Chapter 25 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Proverbs Chapter 25.

questions.question: Who copied out the proverbs of Solomon mentioned in Proverbs 25?
options: The men of Hezekiah king of Judah
The men of David king of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The men of Hezekiah king of Judah
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out' the proverbs, confirming the correct answer.

questions.question: What is said to be the glory of God in Proverbs 25:2?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states, 'It is the glory of God to conceal a thing', making this the correct answer.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:3, what aspect of kings is described as unsearchable?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'the heart of kings is unsearchable', which directly identifies the correct answer.

questions.question: In Proverbs 25:4, what should be taken away from silver to produce a vessel for the finer?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions 'Take away the dross from the silver', confirming that 'the dross' is the correct answer.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:5 suggest should be removed for a king's throne to be established in righteousness?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'Take away the wicked from before the king', directly indicating that 'the wicked' is the correct answer.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:6, where should you not put forth yourself?
options: In the presence of the king
questions.correctAnswer: In the presence of the king
questions.explanation: The verse clearly advises not to 'Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king', making this the correct answer.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 25:7 advises it is better to be invited up rather than be put lower in the presence of a prince.
questions.explanation: The verse states 'For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower', confirming the statement is true.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 25:8 encourages going forth hastily to strive.
questions.explanation: The verse warns 'Go not forth hastily to strive', indicating the statement is false.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:9 suggest one should do when debating a cause?
questions.explanation: The verse advises to 'Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself', making this the correct choice.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:11, what is a word fitly spoken compared to?
options: Apples of gold in pictures of silver
questions.correctAnswer: Apples of gold in pictures of silver
questions.explanation: The verse states 'A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver', confirming the correct answer.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 25:12 compares a wise reprover to fine gold.
questions.explanation: The verse states 'As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover', confirming the statement is true.

questions.question: In Proverbs 25:10, what is likely to happen if you discover a secret to another?
options: You will put yourself to shame
questions.correctAnswer: You will put yourself to shame
questions.explanation: The verse warns 'Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame', indicating the correct answer.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:16 warn against when eating honey?
questions.explanation: The verse advises 'eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith', confirming the correct answer.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:19, what is confidence in an unfaithful man compared to?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth', confirming the correct answer.

medium.title: Proverbs Chapter 25 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Proverbs Chapter 25 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What is the comparison made in Proverbs 25:11 about a word fitly spoken?
options: Apples of gold in pictures of silver
questions.correctAnswer: Apples of gold in pictures of silver
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:11 states that 'A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver,' illustrating the beauty and value of well-timed words.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:12, how is a wise reprover described?
options: As an earring of gold and an ornament of fine gold
questions.correctAnswer: As an earring of gold and an ornament of fine gold
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:12 compares a wise reprover to 'an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold,' signifying their value to those who listen.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:13 say about a faithful messenger?
options: He is like cold of snow in harvest
He is a source of confusion
questions.correctAnswer: He is like cold of snow in harvest
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:13 states, 'As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger,' indicating the refreshing nature of a reliable messenger.

questions.question: In Proverbs 25:14, what is said about those who boast of a false gift?
options: They are like clouds and wind without rain
questions.correctAnswer: They are like clouds and wind without rain
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:14 illustrates that boasting of a false gift is as unfulfilling as 'clouds and wind without rain,' suggesting emptiness.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:15 indicate about the power of patience and a soft tongue?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:15 states that 'By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone,' emphasizing the effectiveness of gentle persuasion.

questions.question: What warning is given in Proverbs 25:16 regarding honey?
options: Eat as much as you want
Only eat it in the morning
Eat so much as is sufficient, lest you be filled and vomit
questions.correctAnswer: Eat so much as is sufficient, lest you be filled and vomit
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:16 advises moderation in consuming honey, warning that overindulgence can lead to discomfort.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:18, what is the consequence of bearing false witness?
options: It is likened to a maul, a sword, and a sharp arrow
It is a sign of wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: It is likened to a maul, a sword, and a sharp arrow
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:18 compares bearing false witness to dangerous weapons, highlighting its destructive nature.

questions.question: What analogy does Proverbs 25:19 use to describe confidence in an unfaithful man?
options: Like a broken tooth and a foot out of joint
questions.correctAnswer: Like a broken tooth and a foot out of joint
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:19 illustrates that trusting an unfaithful person in trouble is as painful as physical injuries, indicating the extent of disappointment.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:20, what is the effect of singing songs to a heavy heart?
options: It is like taking away a garment in cold weather
questions.correctAnswer: It is like taking away a garment in cold weather
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:20 suggests that singing to someone in sorrow can be as distressing as removing their warmth, showing insensitivity.

questions.question: If thine enemy is hungry, what does Proverbs 25:21 instruct you to do?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:21 teaches that one should show kindness to an enemy by providing basic needs, promoting reconciliation.

questions.question: Is it true that Proverbs 25:24 states it is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop than with a brawling woman?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:24 asserts that living in a confined space is preferable to being in conflict with a quarrelsome person, emphasizing the value of peace.

questions.question: Does Proverbs 25:27 suggest that seeking one's own glory is a good pursuit?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:27 indicates that it is not good for men to search their own glory, implying that humility is more virtuous.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:28, a person without self-control is compared to what?
options: A city that is broken down
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:28 states that a person who lacks self-control is like a broken city, emphasizing the importance of maintaining one's spirit.

hard.title: Proverbs Chapter 25 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Proverbs Chapter 25.

questions.question: What should you do if your enemy is hungry according to Proverbs 25:21?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:21 states, 'If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink.' This emphasizes the importance of kindness even towards one's enemies.

questions.question: What is promised if you give food and drink to your enemy according to Proverbs 25:22?
options: You will be rewarded by the LORD
You will bring shame upon yourself
questions.correctAnswer: You will be rewarded by the LORD
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:22 says, 'For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.' This indicates that acts of kindness can lead to divine reward.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:24, where is it better to dwell than with a brawling woman?
options: In a corner of the housetop
questions.correctAnswer: In a corner of the housetop
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:24 states, 'It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house,' highlighting the value of peace over comfort.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:26 compare a righteous man falling before the wicked to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:26 says, 'A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring,' indicating that it disrupts the natural order.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in Proverbs 25:21, comparing giving to an enemy with the act of heaping coals of fire?
questions.explanation: The verse uses metaphor to illustrate the surprising effect of kindness towards an enemy, represented by 'heaping coals of fire upon his head.'

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:27 indicate about seeking one's own glory?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:27 states, 'It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory,' suggesting humility over self-seeking.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:19, what is confidence in an unfaithful man compared to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:19 states, 'Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint,' emphasizing the pain of misplaced trust.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:20 compare to singing songs to a heavy heart?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:20 states, 'As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to a heavy heart,' illustrating the discomfort it causes.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 25:15 states that a soft tongue can break a bone.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:15 says, 'By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone,' indicating the power of gentle communication.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 25:23 claims that an angry countenance can drive away rain.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:23 states, 'The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue,' indicating the negative effect of anger.

questions.question: Which scripture in the New Testament reflects the theme of kindness to enemies found in Proverbs 25:21?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:20 reflects this theme by stating to feed your enemy if they are hungry, echoing Proverbs 25:21’s call for kindness.

questions.question: In Proverbs 25:22, what is the significance of 'heaping coals of fire' in relation to contrasting biblical themes of judgment and mercy?
options: It shows the futility of kindness
questions.explanation: Heaping coals of fire symbolizes the transformative power of kindness that can lead to divine reward, reflecting God's mercy even in judgment.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew word for 'spirit' in Proverbs 25:28 that emphasizes self-control, and what does it imply?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Ruach' means spirit or breath and implies the importance of self-control, as stated in Proverbs 25:28, which compares a lack of control to a broken city.

theological.title: Proverbs Chapter 25 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Proverbs Chapter 25 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the glory of God according to Proverbs 25:2?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:2 states, 'It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.' This verse highlights God's sovereignty and the mystery of His purposes.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:4, what happens when dross is taken away from silver?
options: It becomes a vessel for the finer
questions.correctAnswer: It becomes a vessel for the finer
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:4 says, 'Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.' This illustrates the refining process necessary for purity.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:10 warn against when discussing a secret with others?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:10 states, 'Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.' This warns against the consequences of gossip and betrayal.

questions.question: What does a faithful messenger bring according to Proverbs 25:13?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:13 states, 'As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.' This shows the value of loyalty and faithfulness.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 25:21, what should you do if your enemy is hungry?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:21 instructs, 'If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink.' This reflects the principle of overcoming evil with good.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:15 teach about persuasion?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:15 states, 'By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.' This emphasizes the power of patience and gentle speech.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:26 illustrate about a righteous man?
options: He is like a troubled fountain
He is like a strong fortress
He is like a wise leader
He is like a gentle breeze
questions.correctAnswer: He is like a troubled fountain
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:26 states, 'A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.' This metaphor shows the impact of righteousness in a corrupt context.

questions.question: What warning does Proverbs 25:17 provide regarding visiting neighbors?
options: Stay as long as you wish
Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house
Invite them to your house instead
questions.correctAnswer: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:17 advises, 'Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.' This emphasizes the importance of respecting boundaries.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:6 caution against in the presence of a king?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:6 states, 'Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men.' This warns against pride and presumption.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:19 compare confidence in an unfaithful man to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:19 states, 'Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.' This illustrates the pain and disappointment of misplaced trust.

questions.question: What is the significance of a wise reprover according to Proverbs 25:12?
options: They are a source of conflict
They are like an ornament of fine gold
questions.correctAnswer: They are like an ornament of fine gold
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:12 states, 'As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.' This indicates the value of proper correction.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:22 promise to those who help their enemies?
options: They will be rewarded by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They will be rewarded by the LORD
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:22 states, 'For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.' This teaches that acts of kindness can lead to divine favor.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 25:24 state about living with a brawling woman?
options: It is preferable to live in a palace
It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop
It is the best way to find peace
questions.correctAnswer: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:24 states, 'It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.' This stresses the value of peace over luxury.

questions.question: What insight does Proverbs 25:27 give regarding glory?
options: Men should seek their own glory
It is not good to eat much honey
Men should boast of their achievements
questions.correctAnswer: It is not good to eat much honey
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:27 says, 'It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.' This warns against excessive self-promotion.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the Bible promotes self-centeredness. What does Proverbs 25:27 actually teach?
options: Moderation in all things is important
Seeking one's own glory is encouraged
Boasting is a sign of strength
questions.correctAnswer: Moderation in all things is important
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:27 cautions that 'It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.' This clearly teaches the importance of moderation and humility.
